questions.subject: Commerce
questions.prompt: A student writing a business plan for a new tutoring service wants to note that 'competing tutoring centres charge $40/hour' and 'demand for tutoring is rising in this suburb'. Which section of the plan should this information go in?
options: Market analysis
SWOT analysis
Executive summary
Financial plan
questions.why: Facts about competitors, customers, and demand describe the external market — that's market analysis. SWOT is a separate internal/external judgement tool (strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats) used to evaluate the business itself, not to report raw market facts.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Weimar Republic's constitution is often described as very democratic but also unstable. What made it unstable?
options: Proportional representation made it hard for any one party to gain a strong majority, leading to weak coalition governments
The Kaiser retained full control over all laws
Only wealthy landowners were allowed to vote
Germany had no elected parliament at all
questions.answer: Proportional representation made it hard for any one party to gain a strong majority, leading to weak coalition governments
questions.why: Weimar's proportional representation system meant seats matched vote share closely, but this fragmented parliament into many small parties, forcing shaky coalitions that struggled to govern decisively.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Which best explains why rising unemployment during the Great Depression pushed many Germans toward the Nazi Party specifically, rather than just increasing general anger at the government?
options: The Nazis offered a clear, confident-sounding plan (jobs, national pride, blaming scapegoats) when mainstream parties looked weak and indecisive
The Nazis were the only party allowed to campaign during the Depression
Unemployment had no real connection to which party people supported
The Nazis promised to keep the Weimar constitution exactly as it was
questions.answer: The Nazis offered a clear, confident-sounding plan (jobs, national pride, blaming scapegoats) when mainstream parties looked weak and indecisive
questions.why: It's not just that people were angry — desperate voters were drawn to the Nazis because they projected strength and simple solutions while Weimar coalition governments seemed paralysed and ineffective.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: A government scheme after WWII offers assisted passage to attract skilled British workers to Australia, while at the same time Australia's growing factories need more labour. Which best describes this pairing?
options: The scheme is a pull factor, and the labour shortage is a related pull factor — both draw migrants toward Australia
The scheme is a push factor because it pushes workers out of Britain
Both are push factors because they originate from government policy
Neither is a push or pull factor since assisted migration doesn't count
questions.answer: The scheme is a pull factor, and the labour shortage is a related pull factor — both draw migrants toward Australia
questions.why: Pull factors are reasons that attract people to a destination. Government incentives and job opportunities in Australia both operate on the 'pull' side, not the 'push' side (which would be conditions driving people away from Britain).

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A closed cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 10 cm. What is its total surface area? (Use π ≈ 3.14, round to 1 decimal place)
questions.why: Total surface area = 2πr² + 2πrh = 2(3.14)(9) + 2(3.14)(3)(10) = 56.5 + 188.4 = 244.9 cm². A common mistake is forgetting the two circular ends and only calculating the curved surface (188.4 cm²).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: A country's population living in cities rises sharply as people move from farms to work in city factories. What is this process called, and how does it differ from migration?
options: Urbanisation — it's the shift of population toward cities, which can happen through internal movement, not just international migration
Urbanisation — it only counts if people cross an international border
Migration — urbanisation and migration mean exactly the same thing
Urbanisation — it refers only to farms becoming bigger, not population movement
questions.answer: Urbanisation — it's the shift of population toward cities, which can happen through internal movement, not just international migration
questions.why: Urbanisation is the growing proportion of people living in cities, often driven by internal (within-country) movement. Migration is a broader term covering any movement of people, including between countries — the two overlap but aren't identical.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: When a virus enters the body, white blood cells called lymphocytes produce antibodies. What is the main job of these antibodies?
options: To specifically recognise and bind to the pathogen, marking it for destruction
To physically swallow and digest the pathogen whole
To repair damaged tissue after infection
To carry oxygen to fight the infection faster
questions.answer: To specifically recognise and bind to the pathogen, marking it for destruction
questions.why: Antibodies are proteins shaped to match specific antigens on a pathogen's surface; they bind to it and flag it for other immune cells to destroy. Swallowing pathogens whole is the job of phagocytes, not antibodies.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 9 cm and a height of 8 cm. Work through it calmly: what is its area?
options: 36 cm²
72 cm²
17 cm²
34 cm²
questions.why: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 9 × 8 = 36 cm². Rushing often causes forgetting the ½ (giving 72) or adding base and height instead of multiplying (giving 17). Slow, steady steps avoid both.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.prompt: A new bakery's plan lists: 'local competitors charge $5 for a loaf' and 'weekly foot traffic in this street is high.' Which part of the plan does this information belong in?
options: Market analysis
SWOT analysis
Mission statement
Break-even analysis
questions.why: These are external facts about competitors and customer traffic — core market analysis content. SWOT would instead judge how the bakery's own strengths or weaknesses interact with such conditions, not simply state the facts.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Historians often call the Weimar Republic 'a democracy born from defeat.' What does this phrase mean?
options: It was created after Germany's WWI loss, which many Germans associated with humiliation rather than genuine democratic choice
It means Germany won WWI and then chose democracy freely
It means the Weimar Republic existed before WWI even began
It means the military created Weimar to replace democracy
questions.answer: It was created after Germany's WWI loss, which many Germans associated with humiliation rather than genuine democratic choice
questions.why: The Weimar Republic was established in the shadow of Germany's 1918 defeat and the harsh Treaty of Versailles, so many citizens linked democracy itself with national humiliation, undermining its legitimacy from the start.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Which statement best explains the link between the Great Depression and the Nazi Party's rise, rather than just describing that both happened around the same time?
options: Mass unemployment discredited the mainstream Weimar parties, letting the Nazis present themselves as a strong alternative
The Great Depression made Germans wealthier, so they had free time to attend Nazi rallies
The Great Depression happened after Hitler was already Chancellor
The Great Depression only affected the USA, not Germany
questions.answer: Mass unemployment discredited the mainstream Weimar parties, letting the Nazis present themselves as a strong alternative
questions.why: It's the causal chain that matters: economic collapse weakened trust in existing leadership, creating space for the Nazis' confident promises to gain traction — not just coincidence in timing.
